classification.difficultyReason: Connect even symmetry to retaining and reflecting either half of the graph, and distinguish these input transformations from taking absolute values of outputs.

content.prompt: Suppose that $f$ is even. Which absolute value transformation (if any) will have no effect on the graph?

answer.short: $y=f(|x|)$; also $y=f(-|x|)$. Both leave an even function unchanged.
answer.worked:
An even function has symmetry about the $y$-axis. Keeping either half and reflecting a copy across the $y$-axis reproduces the original graph. Thus $f(|x|)=f(x)$ and $f(-|x|)=f(x)$ wherever $f$ is defined.

The output transformation $y=|f(x)|$ need not leave the graph unchanged: it reflects any negative outputs upwards.
